topic: M-06 durability and outbox refinement boundaries

groups.title: Workbench Store / outbox / Native / Record → pinned DSH persistence

workbench.retrieval: git show from designated mechanisms worktree; no product import or execution

claims: Per-instance Promise queue; clone/mutate/write temporary file/rename/publish; no explicit sync or cross-instance CAS.
Local state and relay intent share Store change in start/report.
Delivery precedes separate sent marker write; catch also covers marker failure.
Recovery intentionally gates worker redelivery; lead relay can retry same outbox ID via retry_delivery.
Dispatch duplicate-key check precedes queue critical section.
Delivery dedup uses history/live-inbox message IDs; early return skips flush.
New relay preserves agent-message provenance, calls followup, then service-wide persistence.flush.
Synchronous model publishes in-memory state/journal/request receipt; duplicate exact command returns historical receipt.
Dispatch changes model state, does not call real network.
Full journal replay rebuilds receipt identities; snapshot installation is a read-cache operation.
Explicitly excludes persistence, actor authentication, cross-process locking and host tool interception.
Constructs Store and Projects; does not integrate Record kernel into native relay or persistence.
Same-dispatch-key test is sequential; native relay test uses mock successful no-op flush; this is not runtime durability proof.

workbench.remote_commit_availability: Not rechecked in this task; source evidence comes from fixed local git objects.

dsh.retrieval: Read public fixed raw source; no third-party code executed

claims: append visibility versus flush durability; flush covers active owned write handles and aggregates failures.
Acknowledged append visibility is weaker than flush durability; close completes pending durability by contract.
followup calls send, which synchronously splices inbox and wakes driver.
Inbox splice appends a session event, then emits insertion notifications.
Session append commits the event to in-memory log and invokes contained observers; no await for storage here.
snapshotEvents reads a frozen copy of the current in-memory log, not an independent persisted read.
Live event copies are buffered; failed drain restores batch and pauses timed drain.
Service flush drains each active writer and aggregates errors, including unrelated sessions.
JSONL delegates service flush to tracker; POSIX materialization syncs file and directory; append syncs and attempts rollback on error.

limits: Static conditions only, no reproduced fault or data-loss incident.
Actual loaded host backend and writer routing not verified; JSONL failure does not necessarily mean target event absent, especially if rollback itself fails.
Do not generalize workbench Store's lack of explicit sync to DSH JSONL, which contains sync mechanisms.
Fresh process recovery, OS/power failure and external-effect verification have separate assumptions.

groups.title: Node.js v24.10.0 File system API
groups.reading_coverage: Targeted writeFile and FileHandle.sync sections, including flush introduction/default and implementation caveat.
claims: writeFile flush defaults false; true invokes filehandle.sync after successful write.
FileHandle.sync asks for storage-device flush with OS/device-specific implementation.
Concurrent writes require synchronization; a Promise completion is not automatically a cross-process transaction.
limits: Not a verification of the currently installed Node or storage device.
No filesystem experiment run; adding flush:true alone does not prove directory namespace durability.

groups.title: Linux man-pages rename(2) and fsync(2)
groups.author_or_institution: Linux man-pages project; man7.org rendering by Michael Kerrisk
groups.reading_coverage: rename DESCRIPTION and NFS BUGS; fsync DESCRIPTION, errors and implementation cautions; version colophons.
claims: Existing target rename is atomic for path lookup under documented semantics.
File fsync does not necessarily flush the containing directory entry; directory sync is separate.
On NFS, a failed rename response cannot establish that no rename occurred.
limits: Linux interface reference, not empirical macOS/APFS or all-device assurance.
Current HTML URL is mutable; displayed manual version/date were recorded.
Open Group POSIX pages returned 403 during discovery; no claim relies on unread POSIX source.

groups.title: Transactional outbox pattern
groups.reading_coverage: Intent, motivation, issues and outbox-table explanation; no example code executed.
claims: Commit business update and outbox event in the same local transaction; a separate relay delivers it.
Duplicate notifications remain possible and require consumer-level handling.
limits: AWS examples do not prove workbench file transaction durability.
Do not generalize wording about FIFO queues to arbitrary business external effects or claim universal exactly-once.
Unversioned live guidance; no publication date was inferred.
